run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:50:21Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is backed by a real, brief error-span burst on frontend-proxy: the ingress error-span ratio rose from about 0.0004-0.0007 to about 0.0366 for 23:55-23:58 and fell back to about 0.0018 at 23:59. In the same interval, frontend's own spans on /api/cart, /api/checkout and its gRPC CartService/CheckoutService client calls carried errors. The cart Deployment was rolled out at 23:52:51-23:52:54 (new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d replacing cart-755465879b; one replica, no readiness probe). The best-supported root-cause candidate is the otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config, whose cartFailure setting is on ('Fail cart service'); the cart rollout is the likely mechanism and the frontend/frontend-proxy errors its consequences. Conclusion is partial because the flag value actually in effect at 23:52 cannot be verified, cart's own spans show no error status, and the alert's exact expression/value could not be reproduced. The fraud-detection OOM restart is a separate event, not the cause of this cart-related burst.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error-span rate was 0 for ingress and router frontend egress until 23:50:21, then jumped to about 0.35 spans/s for both operations at 23:54:21-23:58:21 (ingress 0.3519-0.3630/s, router frontend egress 0.3444/s), before returning to background.
The ingress-only error-span ratio for frontend-proxy was 0.000375-0.000750 at 23:50:00-23:54:00, rose to 0.0363-0.0366 at 23:55:00-23:58:00, and fell to 0.001842 at 23:59:00.

frontend's own error spans in the burst included executing api route (pages) /api/cart at 0.2778/s, POST /api/cart at 0.1926/s, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem at 0.1926/s, GET /api/cart and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart at 0.0852/s, POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder at 0.0667/s, and tcp.connect at 0.0259/s at 23:54:21-23:58:21.

No cart server-operation span series carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the returned cart metrics; POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, AddItem, EmptyCart, HGET, HMSET and EXPIRE were returned as STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and the only cart error series returned (flagd EventStream) was 0 at 23:54:21-00:00:21.

The cart Deployment was rolled out at 23:52:51-23:52:54: it scaled new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1, started pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz, stopped container cart in old pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4, and scaled old ReplicaSet cart-755465879b from 1 to 0.
The cart Deployment is at generation 2 and its pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:52:51Z; its current image is ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart.
The cart Deployment uses RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25%, has no readinessProbe and no minReadySeconds, and runs one replica.
The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config declares cartFailure with defaultVariant on, description 'Fail cart service', and state ENABLED.

The same flagd-config sets adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure to off or numeric-off default variants.

The flagd pod started at 23:23:36 with 0 restarts; its init container copies /config-ro/demo.flagd.json to /config-rw/demo.flagd.json once at pod start, and flagd is started with --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json.

The fraud-detection pod's fraud-detection container last terminated with reason OOMKilled and exit code 137 at 2026-11-17T23:58:21Z, and its restart count is 1; its container was started again at 23:58:22.

The frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt and the new cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz were Running, ready, and had 0 restarts when checked; the cart Service had exactly one ready endpoint pointing at cart-84889c965d-tkxdz.

The errors are connection-level rather than cart in-process errors: cart server spans carry no error status while frontend's tcp.connect and CartService client spans fail, and the burst begins immediately after the single-replica cart pod replacement, which has no readiness probe or minReadySeconds.

The flagd value actually in effect at 23:52 is not established: flagd started at 23:23:36 from a one-time file copy made by its init container, so a ConfigMap edit after that time would not be read without a flagd restart, and no flagd restart is visible in the incident events or pod status.

The fraud-detection OOM restart did not cause this frontend-proxy error burst: the ingress error ratio was already 0.0363-0.0366 at 23:55-23:58 before the OOMKilled termination at 23:58:21, and no fraud-detection error spans were returned in the burst interval.

The cartFailure setting held in flagd-config is the injected fault: its description 'Fail cart service' names the cart workload that was rolled out with a restartedAt annotation at 23:52:51, no other change-applying object is visible, and the frontend's cart/checkout client spans and frontend-proxy ingress errors are the consequences, with the cart rollout as the mechanism.

An alternative mechanism remains: the one-replica cart Deployment rollout itself created a short endpoint/startup gap (old pod stopped at 23:52:54, new pod started at 23:52:51-23:52:53 with no readiness probe), causing connection-level UNAVAILABLE/tcp.connect failures from frontend; the flag's role is unverified.

Confirm the effective flagd configuration and the history of the cartFailure setting; if cart failure is not intended, set cartFailure back to off and refresh or restart flagd so the setting takes effect.
Add a readiness probe and minReadySeconds to the cart container and use maxUnavailable: 0 for its single-replica rollout, so frontend keeps a ready cart endpoint during replacement.
Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its data source, since the 0.0111 value in the alert could not be reproduced from the available frontend-proxy series.

gaps: change_history is not integrated, so it is unknown who or what set kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:52:51Z on the cart Deployment or when the cartFailure value in flagd-config was changed.
The flagd flag value actually in effect at 23:52 is unknown: flagd started at 23:23:36 from a one-time copy of the ConfigMap, and no flagd restart is visible.
Jaeger returned no traces for 23:53-23:59 (the error window), so the error status text and exact failing request details for the frontend/cart errors were not available.
Frontend application logs returned no lines for the incident window, and the cart log query filtered for fail/error/exception returned no failure lines; the alleged cart exception was not observed.
list_prometheus_rules for RequestErrorRate returned no rule, so the exact alert expression and the annotation value 0.0111 could not be verified.
kube_replicaset_owner returned no series for cart, so the ReplicaSet ownership evidence comes from Kubernetes events and deployment metadata rather than that metric.
The incident-window event list does not show a flagd restart or any change object other than the cart Deployment, but events can expire and were not exhaustive.
next_steps: Check the change/audit history for flagd-config and the cart Deployment around 23:50-23:53 to confirm the trigger of the restartedAt annotation and the cartFailure edit.
Inspect the flagd process state or its loaded /config-rw/demo.flagd.json to verify whether cartFailure was on before and during the burst.
Inspect the RequestErrorRate alert rule and its source so the alert value 0.0111 can be reconciled with the frontend-proxy series.
Review the cart and frontend logs from the burst window with broader filters, and capture the gRPC status codes for the failed CartService calls.
